# Churchill Downs Stars of Tomorrow II Stakes Advances: Coach Pope Takes On Staunch in Kentucky Jockey Club


## Nov 21, 2026


Grade I-placed Coach Pope and Street Sense (Grade III) runner-up Staunch lead a competitive cast of 11 2-year-olds entered for the 100th running of the $400,000 Kentucky Jockey Club (GII) next Saturday at Churchill Downs.


The 1 1/16-mile Kentucky Jockey Club is one of four stakes on the 12-race Stars of Tomorrow II program, which is devoted exclusively to 2-year-olds. Also on the card are the $400,000 Fasig-Tipton Golden Rod (GII) and $225,000 Fern Creek (Listed) for fillies and the $225,000 Ed Brown for open company. First post is 1 p.m. (all times Eastern) with the Kentucky Jockey Club scheduled as Race 12 at 6:26 p.m.


Trained by Kenny McPeek for Gainesway Stable, Shamrock Stables and Mike Mackin, Coach Pope returns to Churchill Downs, where he dominated a one-mile maiden special weight by 12 ½ lengths Sept. 12. The son of Tapit followed that performance with a runner-up finish to American History in the Breeders’ Futurity (GI) at Keeneland before finishing fourth in the Breeders’ Cup Juvenile (GI) over the same track Oct. 30. Manny Esquivel has the mount in the Kentucky Jockey Club from post No. 2.


McPeek also entered Bayview Stables, Mark Edwards and Mike Trout’s Real Goodbar, who returns to dirt following his victory in the Oct. 30 Thoroughbred Aftercare Alliance Stakes on turf at Keeneland. Luis Saez rides from post 9.


McPeek is a three-time winner of the Kentucky Jockey Club with victories by Repent (2001), Signalman (2018) and Smile Happy (2021). A victory Saturday would tie Hall of Fame trainer D. Wayne Lukas’ race record of four wins.


Bourbon Fueled Racing’s Staunch narrowly missed his first stakes victory when he finished a neck behind Jas in the Oct. 25 Street Sense at Churchill Downs. Trained by Brendan Walsh, the son of Liam’s Map earned his maiden win by four lengths going 7 ½ furlongs Sept. 26 beneath the Twin Spires before stretching out to two turns in the Street Sense. Tyler Gaffalione, aboard for both efforts, will ride Staunch from post 8.


Also entered in the race are Saints or Sinners’ undefeated Bowman Mill winner Just for Pipa; Asagi Stables’ Keeneland allowance winner Showa; and Jackpot Farm and Spendthrift Farm’s eye-catching maiden winner Fools Rush In.


The complete lineup for the Kentucky Jockey Club from the rail out (with jockey and trainer):


Asap (Axel Concepcion, Dallas Stewart)
Coach Pope (Esquivel, McPeek)
Start the Disco (Alex Achard, Riley Mott)
Staunch (Gaffalione, Walsh)
Braums Run (Walter Rodriguez, Mark Casse)
Just for Pipa (Edgar Morales, Greg Foley)
Fools Rush In (Flavien Prat, Brad Cox)
Monnie (Keith Asmussen, Steve Asmussen)
Real Goodbar (Saez, McPeek)
Full Access (Jaime Torres, Riley Mott)
Showa (Jose Ortiz, Wesley Ward)
The Road to the Kentucky Derby presented by Woodford Reserve returns to Churchill Downs with the Kentucky Jockey Club, which awards qualifying points to the top five finishers on a 10-5-3-2-1 scale toward a spot in the starting gate for the 153rd running of the $5 million Kentucky Derby presented by Woodford Reserve (GI) on Saturday, May 1.


Since their introduction in 2005, Churchill Downs’ Stars of Tomorrow programs have helped launch the careers of 103 Grade I or Group I winners, including four Kentucky Derby winners and eight Kentucky Oaks winners. Alumni include Derby winners Super Saver, Mandaloun, Mystik Dan and Sovereignty, along with Eclipse Award champions Rachel Alexandra, Gun Runner, Monomoy Girl and Thorpedo Anna.


RAGS TO RICHES WINNER WHARFIE LEADS $400,000 FASIG-TIPTON GOLDEN ROD – Godolphin’s Rags to Riches winner Wharfie will attempt to give the operation a third consecutive victory in the $400,000 Fasig-Tipton Golden Rod (Grade II) when she faces seven fellow 2-year-old fillies in the race’s 83rd running next Saturday at Churchill Downs.


The 1 1/16-mile Fasig-Tipton Golden Rod goes as Race 10 at 5:25 p.m. First post is 1 p.m.


Trained by Hall of Famer Bill Mott, Wharfie rallied from last of seven under Junior Alvarado to defeat Juana Margarita by three-quarters of a length in the Oct. 25 Rags to Riches at Churchill Downs. That victory followed a 2 ¾-length maiden special weight win going one mile Sept. 19 at Belmont Park. A daughter of Essential Quality, Wharfie has won two of three starts and earned $180,740. Alvarado retains the mount and the duo will break from post No. 8.


Godolphin won the last two editions of the Golden Rod with Good Cheer in 2024 and Bella Ballerina in 2025. Mott will seek his third victory in the race after winning with Gold Sunrise in 1995 and Carina Mia in 2015.


Also entered in the race are David Bernsen and Steve Crabtree’s Rags to Riches runner-up Juana Margarita; LNJ Foxwoods and Church Street Stable’s debut winner Breezy; and Shortleaf Stable’s Tiger Baby, who scored an impressive five-length maiden victory Friday at Churchill Downs.


The field for the Golden Rod in order of post position (with jockey and trainer):


Spectacular Sam (Luis Saez, Robbie Medina)
Dazzling (Jose Ortiz, Steve Asmussen)
Juana Margarita (Manny Esquivel, Kenny McPeek)
Breezy (Flavien Prat, Will Walden)
Tulsi (Walter Rodriguez, Jason DaCosta)
Stand by Me (Tyler Gaffalione, Eric Foster)
Tiger Baby (Manny Esquivel, Kenny McPeek)
Wharfie (Alvarado, Mott)
Named for Kentucky’s state flower, the Golden Rod was first contested in 1910. Its winners include Hall of Famers Silverbulletday (1998) and Rachel Alexandra (2008), who both returned the following spring to win the Longines Kentucky Oaks (GI), the same path Good Cheer followed with her Oaks victory in 2025.


The Fasig-Tipton Golden Rod is part of the Road to the Kentucky Oaks and awards qualifying points to the top five finishers on a 10-5-3-2-1 scale toward a spot in the starting gate for the 153rd Longines Kentucky Oaks on Friday, April 30.


SANFORD WINNER BOOKED LEADS $225,000 ED BROWN – Jackpot Farm, Alvin Fults, Jason Itkin and Michael Smith’s Sanford (Grade III) winner Booked leads a competitive cast of 11 2-year-olds entered for the sixth running of the $225,000 Ed Brown next Saturday at Churchill Downs.


The 6 ½-furlong Ed Brown is one of four stakes on the 12-race Stars of Tomorrow II program, which is devoted exclusively to 2-year-olds. The field will go to post at 5:54 p.m. in Race 11.


Trained by Hall of Famer Steve Asmussen, Booked won the July 4 Sanford at Saratoga by six lengths before finishing second in the Saratoga Special (GII) and third in the Hopeful (GI). He enters the Ed Brown following a third-place finish as the 3-5 favorite in the Oct. 24 Bowman Mill at Keeneland. Jockey Flavien Prat has the mount from post No. 5.


Asmussen also entered the Estate of Mike McCarty’s Grand Yaupon, who won the Sept. 27 Clever Trevor at Prairie Meadows and finished second in the Ellis Park Juvenile earlier this summer. Keith Asmussen rides from post 3.


Also entered are familiar rivals Chancery and Dormie, who met in an Oct. 3 allowance at Keeneland. Ceahorse and Highland Yard’s Chancery won that race by 3 ¼ lengths to remain unbeaten in two starts for trainer Rusty Arnold II. Richard Perkins’ Dormie, trained by Chris Block, returned to dominate an allowance there by 9 ¾ lengths Oct. 30.


Axel Concepcion rides Chancery from post 4 while Luis Saez has the mount on Dormie from post 6.


The field for the Ed Brown from the rail out (with jockey and trainer):


Merit Badge (Constantino Roman, Anna Meah)
Bearamour (Jaime Torres, Keith Desormeaux)
Grand Yaupon (Asmussen, Asmussen)
Chancery (Concepcion, Arnold)
Booked (Prat, Asmussen)
Dormie (Saez, Block)
McCoy (Jose Ortiz, Cherie DeVaux)
National Forest (Tyler Gaffalione, Brad Cox)
Teacher (Brian Hernandez Jr., Jerry Dixon Jr.)
Into Music (Fausto DaSilva, Tena Birdwell)
Title Worthy (Gerardo Corrales, Dallas Stewart)
The Ed Brown Stakes honors Hall of Famer Edward Dudley Brown, who trained 1877 Kentucky Derby winner Baden-Baden and won the Belmont Stakes as a jockey. Brown was inducted into the National Museum of Racing’s Hall of Fame in 1984.


MYRTLEWOOD WINNER STRESS RELIEF LEADS $225,000 FERN CREEK – Joel Politi’s homebred Myrtlewood winner Stress Relief will seek her third stakes victory when she leads a field of 10 2-year-old fillies in the sixth running of the $225,000 Fern Creek (Listed) next Saturday at Churchill Downs.


Run at 6 ½ furlongs, the Fern Creek is one of four stakes on the 12-race Stars of Tomorrow II program, which is devoted exclusively to 2-year-olds. The Fern Creek goes as Race 9 of 12 at 4:55 p.m. First post is 1 p.m.


Trained by Kinnon LaRose, Stress Relief rallied to defeat Glory Run by a neck in the Oct. 23 Myrtlewood at Keeneland, with fellow Fern Creek entrant Rescue Dawn another length back in third. The daughter of Not This Time won her June 20 debut at Churchill Downs by five lengths before winning the Aug. 2 Adirondack (GIII) at Saratoga by 3 ½ lengths. That victory gave LaRose, a former assistant to Tom Amoss who opened his stable in March, his first graded stakes win. Jockey Luis Saez has the mount out of post No. 6.


Also entered in the race are recent maiden winners Joyful Flight, who won her debut by 4 ½ lengths at Keeneland for C R K Stable and trainer Peter Eurton; Appeals to Me, who was victorious at second asking for trainer Brad Cox and owners Full of Run Racing, Agile Partners and Gary Garlington; and Forgive Me, who won her second career start by a length for Godolphin and trainer Brendan Walsh.


The complete lineup for the Fern Creek in order of post position (with jockey and trainer):


Forgive Me (Tyler Gaffalione, Walsh)
Elewene (Martin Garcia, Dale Romans)
Appeals to Me (Flavien Prat, Cox)
Cafe Rose (Fausto Da Silva, Tena Birdwell)
Joyful Flight (Jose Ortiz, Eurton)
Stress Relief (Saez, LaRose)
Glory Run (Alex Achard, John Ennis)
Rescue Dawn (Walter Rodriguez, Mike Maker)
Right in Time (Junior Alvarado, Riley Mott)
